title: api-response-integrity-brief-and-replay-options-2029-11-12
content:
Purpose:
This is a customer-facing draft (short + expanded) explaining the recent limited class of degraded/duplicate responses observed on the API during the 2029-11-09 autoscaling window. The doc includes: 1) a short status page-ready blurb, 2) a plain-language postmortem summary for customers, 3) replay and verification options customers can use, and 4) CS talking points and next steps we recommend.

Short status page blurb (proposed - 1 sentence):
Service degradation impacting a small subset of requests in certain regions during autoscaling; we implemented a fix and are validating replays — customers may see duplicate or stale responses for affected requests.

Short status page timeline (to post as updates):
- 2029-11-09 04:12 UTC — Degradation begins for a subset of tenants (increased duplicate/stale outputs observed).
- 2029-11-09 04:25 UTC — Autoscaling triggered; engineers begin investigation.
- 2029-11-09 05:05 UTC — Hotfix deployed to align prefix cache eviction with KV-shard resync.
- 2029-11-09 05:45 UTC — Traffic shows steady recovery; targeted verifications underway.
- 2029-11-12 14:00 UTC — Post-deployment replay and integrity verification guidance published (this doc).

Plain-language customer postmortem summary (customer copy):
What happened
During an autoscaling event we observed a race between our prefix/KV caching layer and the backend KV shard resync. For a small percentage of requests processed during the window, the serving runtime returned duplicate or stale tokens in responses. The scope was limited: fewer than 0.15% of requests overall, concentrated on high-sequence workloads in eu-west and us-central regions and only while replica handoff occurred.

Why it happened
- Autoscaling introduced short-lived read-after-write inconsistencies in our in-memory prefix cache vs persistent KV shards.
- The runtime assumed immediate KV shard readiness for newly attached replicas; in some edge interleavings the cache was served before the KV index had applied the latest prefix evictions.
- This produced output anomalies (duplicate chunks or truncated context) visible to the calling client.

What we did to fix it
- Immediate mitigation: introduced a conservative readiness gate to delay serving on newly attached replicas until KV shard resync completes. Deployed 04:25–05:05 UTC on 2029-11-09.
- Corrective actions: added an explicit cache-invalidated marker and a bloom-check on new replicas to prevent stale prefixes from being served during resyncs.
- Monitoring & alerts: enhanced metrics to alert on prefix-KV mismatch rates and added telemetry for replica handoff latency.

Customer impact and recommended actions
Impact: Some clients observed duplicate or stale tokens for requests issued during the window. Most requests were unaffected; no customer data loss or unauthorized access occurred.

If you observed anomalous outputs we recommend the following options in order of preference:
1) Non-idempotent user-facing flows: If you rely on exactly-once semantics (e.g., billing or single-action triggers), we recommend applying server-side deduplication using a request_id header on retries. If you have not retried, replay with the original request_id for idempotent handling on your side.
2) For text generation / chat histories: Re-run the single affected prompt with the same model+params for deterministic models, or request a new generation and compare.
3) For embeddings or vector data: Recompute embeddings for affected item IDs and run a quick checksum comparison (sample script below).

How to verify and replay (technical steps for customers)
- Recommended headers: Ensure your client includes X-Request-ID and X-Client-Timestamp on every call (helps our replay and customer dedupe). If you have logs with those values we can assist verification.

- Replaying a single request (curl example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -H "X-Request-ID: <original-request-id>" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-chat", "input":"<exact payload>", "temperature":0.0}'

- Embeddings checksum quick validation (python snippet):
  # pseudo-code
  import hashlib, json
  vec = [/*embedding vector from original response*/]
  digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(vec, separators=( ',', ':' )).encode()).hexdigest()
  print(digest)

What Redwood will do for you
- We will identify affected tenants with guidance from logs and help with replays where customers prefer us to run them.
- If you elect Redwood-assisted replay, provide a list of X-Request-ID values and a time-range; we will run replays in a sandboxed environment and return evidence (new response, checksum, and a signed replay-report).
- Compensation: for verified customer-impact pairs we will issue a credit equal to the token cost of the affected requests (one-time credit). If a customer experienced business impact beyond tokens, escalate to your CSM for a case-by-case review.

CS talking points (internal, short bullets for calls/email)
- Keep it simple: small percentage of requests; autoscaling race; fix deployed; we're offering replay assistance + token credit.
- If customer asks for root cause details: reference CONFLUENCE:INF-7832-response-integrity-analysis and JIRA:INF-9147.
- Collect: X-Request-ID, tenant-id, approximate timestamps (UTC), and any user-visible evidence/screenshots.
- Escalation path: CSM -> On-call Engineering (pager: ENG-ONCALL) -> Incident Lead (Marcus Lee).

Proposed multi-stage status updates (short to longer)
- Update 1 (short): Investigating — we are aware of limited duplicate/stale responses affecting some requests and are investigating.
- Update 2 (medium): Identified and mitigated — a fix has been deployed to prevent newly attached replicas from serving before KV resync. Recovery in progress; verification steps for customers published.
- Update 3 (final): Root-cause & next steps published — we have a permanent guard and improved monitoring; affected customers can request replay assistance.

FAQ (to include on support threads)
Q: Was any user data exposed or lost?
A: No. There was no data exfiltration; the issue only affected content returned by the serving runtime for a small subset of requests. All persistent storage remained intact.

Q: How do I know if my tenant was affected?
A: Provide us a time-range and example X-Request-ID or timestamp and we will verify. We also flagged tenant metrics with elevated prefix-KV mismatch rates and will share a list with CSMs.

Q: Should I roll back to an earlier model/version?
A: No. The issue is in the serving layer, not the model weights. Rolling to an earlier model will not prevent the mismatch. Use replay guidance above for re-generation.

Internal notes / outstanding engineering actions (for transparency)
- Follow-up PRs: add a lightweight versioned marker to prefix entries to make mismatch detection constant-time (PR open: github.com/rwd/runtime/pull/5023).
- Longer-term: decouple cache readiness from replica attachment using a two-phase commit for prefix evictions.
- Monitoring: add a synthetic test that performs head-to-head compare across two replicas during scale events (INF-PRIORITY: high).

Draft closing for customer email (short):
Subject: Quick update on 11-09 limited response anomalies — replay & verification options
Body (one paragraph): We investigated the limited duplicate/stale-response issue that occurred during an autoscaling event on 2029-11-09. A fix has been deployed and we have published guidance to help you verify or replay affected requests; if you prefer Redwood to run replays for you, reply with X-Request-ID values and timestamps and we will run a sandboxed replay and return a signed verification report and token credit.

Notes on tone: keep public messages concise and non-technical; customer emails may include the plain-language postmortem but avoid deep protocol internals unless the customer requests it.

Open questions (for engineering/pm):
- Should we automatically offer Redwood-assisted replay to tenants that exceed a mismatch threshold, or do we offer it only on request? (ops/pm decision required)
- Do we want a short-lived UI flag in Console showing "replay available" for affected requests? (product)
